slides.headline:
אמא ואבא
5 דברים שיעזרו לי
להיפרד מהטיטול
הטיטול שלי עוד איתי
slides.body:
אני כבר רצה, מטפסת ושרה,
ועדיין עם טיטול מתחת למכנסיים.
אני רוצה להיות גדולה,
אבל להרגיש מתי בא לי פיפי
זה **חדש** לי לגמרי.

scene.action: The girl runs and climbs on the sofa cushions, laughing, a diaper peeking out above her leggings, her parents watching with a smile.
scene.setting: The family's cosy Israeli living room: a beige sofa, a soft rug, a toy basket, a plain pale wall. The upper third of the frame stays calm: a plain soft background, no faces or hands there.

slides.label: 1: תחתונים של גדולים
slides.headline: אני בוחרת את התחתונים
slides.body:
תחתונים עם תותים, או עם כוכבים?
כשאני בוחרת בעצמי, זה מרגיש שלי.
וכשאני לובשת אותם, אני גדולה **באמת**.
תנו לי לעבור לתחתונים כבר כשמתחילים.

scene.action: The girl holds up two pairs of colourful big-kid underwear, one with strawberries and one with stars, deciding with a serious face, her mother kneeling beside her.
scene.setting: The girl's small Israeli bedroom in the morning: an open drawer, a low bed, a plain pale wall. The upper third of the frame stays calm: a plain soft background, no faces or hands there.

slides.label: 2: רגליים על הרצפה
slides.headline: למה אני קופצת מהאסלה?
slides.body:
האסלה גבוהה, והחור גדול.
הרגליים שלי מתנדנדות באוויר.
## מה יעזור לי:
סיר קטן בגובה שלי,
שהרגליים שלי **נוגעות** ברצפה.

scene.action: The girl sits comfortably on a small potty chair with both feet flat on the floor, a towel over her lap, smiling at her father who crouches nearby.
scene.setting: The family's bright Israeli bathroom: plain pale cream wall tiles, a small potty chair and a step stool by the toilet. The upper third of the frame stays calm: a plain soft background, no faces or hands there.

slides.label: 3: סיר ראשון בבוקר
slides.headline: ספר אחד, וכבר ישבתי
slides.body:
בבוקר, ראשון,
עוד בפיג׳מה,
ישר לסיר.
עם ספר על הברכיים.
דף, ועוד **דף**.

scene.action: In pyjamas, the girl sits on her small potty chair first thing in the morning, a towel over her lap and a picture book open on her knees, sleepy and content.
scene.setting: The family's bright Israeli bathroom: plain pale cream wall tiles, a small potty chair and a step stool by the toilet. The upper third of the frame stays calm: a plain soft background, no faces or hands there.

slides.label: 4: לראות אתכם
slides.headline: אני רוצה לבוא איתכם
slides.body:
אתם נכנסים לשירותים, ואני אחריכם.
אני רוצה לראות מה עושים שם.
## מה יעזור לי:
> ״בואי, הילה, ואחר כך שוטפים ידיים.״
ככה אני רואה איך **גדולים** עושים.

scene.action: The girl and her mother wash their hands side by side at the bathroom sink, the girl standing on a step stool, both covered in soap bubbles.
scene.setting: The family's bright Israeli bathroom: plain pale cream wall tiles, a small potty chair and a step stool by the toilet. The upper third of the frame stays calm: a plain soft background, no faces or hands there.

slides.label: 5: מילה ברורה
slides.headline: ״ישבת לבד על הסיר!״
slides.body:
## מה אתם רואים:
ילדה שקופצת מהסיר בצעקות.
## מה קורה לי בפנים:
אני רוצה שתראו **מה עשיתי**.
## מה יעזור לי:
מילה ברורה על מה שהצלחתי,
בלי ממתק ובלי פרס. זה מספיק לי.

scene.action: The girl jumps up from the potty area with her arms in the air, beaming, while both parents clap and smile in the bathroom doorway.
scene.setting: The family's bright Israeli bathroom: plain pale cream wall tiles, a small potty chair and a step stool by the toilet. The upper third of the frame stays calm: a plain soft background, no faces or hands there.

slides.headline: צעד צעד, בקצב שלי
slides.body:
יהיו פספוסים, ויהיו ימים טובים.
תחתונים, סיר נמוך, ספר בבוקר,
ומילה טובה כשהצלחתי.
ככה אני **נפרדת** מהטיטול.

scene.action: The girl hugs both parents on the hallway rug, wearing her strawberry underwear over her leggings like a proud joke, everyone laughing.
scene.setting: The family's Israeli hallway: a door to the bathroom, a soft rug, a plain pale wall. The upper third of the frame stays calm: a plain soft background, no faces or hands there.

sources.title: The Right Age to Potty Train
sources.quote: Toilet training struggles happen when children choose not to use the toilet. It's important to remember that children can succeed at using the toilet but in their own time. ... Choose the words your family will use to describe body parts, urine, and bowel movements. Avoid words that are negative, like dirty, naughty, or stinky. ... Children's feet should be able to reach the floor. Books or toys for "potty time" may help make this time more fun. ... Let your children see you use the toilet and wash your hands afterward. ... When your children feel the urge to poop, you might notice grunting, squatting, or freezing. ... Explain briefly to your children that these signs mean a poop is about to come. If your children tell you about a wet diaper, praise them for "using their words." ... Talk with them about how they will now be in charge of their pee and poop. Read children's books about using the toilet to help the process make sense and seem inviting and exciting. ... Make a habit of seating your children onto the potty-chair first thing in the morning. ... Gently help them overcome their hesitation. Then help them stay in charge by having them be in charge of the cleanup.
sources.supports: Potty training advice from the AAP: children learn in their own time, positive words, a potty chair where the feet reach the floor, books, a role model, signs of a poop coming, being in charge, a morning routine, hesitation and cleanup. An American page, applied to Israeli families as general child-health advice.

sources.title: Potty Training: 12 Tips to Keep the Process Positive
sources.quote: When toilet training starts, switch to big-kid underwear. ... Be precise with praise. ... Avoid treats and punishments. ... When your children succeed, be specific about why you are proud. ... Avoid a power struggle. ... Try to stay calm about toilet training. Remember that children control when and where they pee and poop. So power struggles, begging, pleading, rewarding, and punishing keep children from managing their own toileting. ... Understand their fear. Some children believe that their pee and poop are part of their bodies. They may be scared the toilet will flush parts of them away. ... To give your children a feeling of control, let them flush the toilet. ... Toilet training is a learning experience.
sources.supports: Big-kid underwear, specific praise without treats, avoiding power struggles, staying calm, fear of the flush and letting the child flush. An American page, applied to Israeli families as general child-health advice.
